predecessors.note: Frederick I of Swabia ceded the Breisgau to Berthold II in 1096 (Duchy of Swabia page); in 1098 Berthold 'reconciled with Frederick, renounced all claims to Swabia' and took the title Duke of Zähringen (House of Zähringen page).

land.text: Zürich and Schaffhausen, partly reverted to the crown or granted imperial immediacy

successors.note: After Berthold V died on 18 February 1218 'the ducal line of the Zähringer became extinct'; some territories reverted to the crown, the allodial titles were divided between the counts of Urach and Kyburg (Fürstenberg on the Berthold V page).
Needs a dossier (Kyburg lands passed largely to the Habsburgs within 50 years).

land.text: the Breisgau around Freiburg and Breisach

successors.note: Urach heirs in the Breisgau (the later Fürstenberg line); needs a dossier.

capitals.name: Freiburg im Breisgau
capitals.note: 'Berthold II moved his main residence to Freiburg Castle' in 1091; Freiburg was founded in 1120 and Berthold V died there in 1218.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Zähringen row; its Holy Roman Empire shape draws the land as imperial). The Breisgau ceded in 1096 is the core: a 45 km circle around Freiburg (about 6,000 km2). The page gives no area. The Zähringer also held imperial jurisdiction over Zürich from 1098 and the Burgundian Rectorate from 1127; those are the vassal tints in the ledger, not direct land.

region.text: the Breisgau around Freiburg and Breisach

ledger.note: 1098: Berthold II becomes Duke of Zähringen. He 'reconciled with Frederick, renounced all claims to Swabia' and took the title Duke of Zähringen, with Zähringen Castle and jurisdiction over Zürich; the Breisgau had been ceded in 1096. He had been elected duke of Swabia against Frederick I in 1092.
1098: the Zähringer receive jurisdiction over Zürich. The page: 'jurisdiction over Zürich' in 1098; they 'held the imperial advocacy' there. Drawn as the lighter tint until the acquisition of 1173.

region.text: the Burgundian lands of the Rectorate: Bern (founded 1191), Fribourg (founded 1157), Thun and the Bernese Oberland, Vaud

ledger.note: 1127: Conrad is made rector of Burgundy. 'Conrad claimed the County of Burgundy inheritance. Lothair III then appointed him rector of the Kingdom of Burgundy-Arles'; the rectorate was confirmed in 1152 and held until 1218. The lands drawn (Bern, Fribourg, Vaud) are the researcher's reading from the cities Berthold IV and V founded.

region.text: the lands south of Lake Geneva

ledger.note: 1156: the lands south of Lake Geneva go to Savoy and Provence. 'Lands south of Lake Geneva were ceded to Savoy and Provence'; the page names no places.
1173: the Zähringer acquire Zürich after the Lenzburg extinction ('Zürich was acquired' in 1173).
1173: Berthold IV acquires Zürich after the Lenzburg line dies out; the Zähringer already held the imperial advocacy.

1198: Philip pays Berthold V 3,000 silver marks for renouncing his claim to the throne. The concessions 'consolidated Zähringer control over the Ortenau, the Breisgau, Schaffhausen, Breisach and All Saints' Abbey'; Schaffhausen is dated 1198 on the House of Zähringen page. The same year Berthold crushed an uprising of the Burgundian nobles.

region.text: the Burgundian lands of the Rectorate: Bern (founded 1191), Fribourg (founded 1157), Thun and the Bernese Oberland, Vaud

ledger.note: 1218: the Burgundian Rectorate ends with the dukes. The rectorate was 'confirmed in 1152' and 'the Zähringer held it until 1218'.

union.text: the Breisgau around Freiburg and Breisach

ledger.note: 1218: Berthold V dies in Freiburg and the ducal line ends. 'with the death of Berthold V in 1218, the younger line of Zähringer dynasty became extinct in the male line'; his son Berthold had died in 1216. His lands were divided between the houses of Urach, Kyburg and Fürstenberg, partly reverted to the crown or were granted imperial immediacy (Bern is a free imperial city by the infobox).

wars.name: Battle of Ulrichen
wars.outcome: Berthold V failed to gain access to the Valais at Ulrichen in 1211 and had to accept Savoyard suzerainty over the upper Valais by the treaty of Hautcret Abbey on 19 October 1211.
wars.note: The Valais was never Zähringer land; no border moved.

certainty.note: No page gives a border; the Breisgau, Ortenau and Burgundian lands are approximated by circles and cantons.

sources.title: Berthold V, Duke of Zähringen

notes: Two pages opened (budget 2-5). The Duchy of Zähringen has no article of its own (it redirects to the House); the dossier's Wikipedia title is 'House of Zähringen'. The Zähringer 'duchy' was a title without a territorial duchy (the Breisgau, Ortenau, Zürich and the Burgundian rectorate); the Rectorate lands are a reading and the 1156 cession is as vague as the page. Not settled: Zürich's status (advocacy 1098 vs acquisition 1173 on the same page), the Ortenau and Schaffhausen dates (1198 as a consolidation), and what Berthold IV held in Burgundy before 1186. The 1096 loss in stem-duchy-of-swabia names 'Berthold II of Zähringen' as counterpart. Counterparts needing dossiers: county-of-kyburg, county-of-urach (Fürstenberg), county-of-savoy (Cliopatria from 1260). Gazetteer lacks Offenburg.
